We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={x}^{2}+1\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2}+1)(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-2\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(1)dx \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,dx \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =({x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-2\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-2(-x\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x+D) \\  & =({x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-2D.$ Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }({x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={[({x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2\operatorname{sin}⁡x]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =({\pi }^{2}+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi +2\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi -2\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi -(({0}^{2}+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡0+2\cdot 0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡0-2\operatorname{sin}⁡0) \\  & =({\pi }^{2}+1)\cdot 0+2\pi (-1)-2\cdot 0-0 \\  & =-2\pi \end{aligned}
$$
